extracted.intended_audience: CIA Office of Security, Office of Legislative Liaison, and agency policymakers reviewing OMB draft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Internal agency memorandum analyzing a draft OMB Circular titled 'Guidelines for Legislation Involving Federal Criminal Law Enforcement Authorities', focusing on delegation of protective responsibility, training/accreditation requirements, and firearms authority for agency personnel (including proposed Access Control Officers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Make a Warrantless Arrest
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 5(c) ('Authority to Make a Warrantless Arrest') requires that the 'employee has completed an accredited course of training in the exercise of the power to arrest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 3(a) defines an 'accredited course of training' as 'A systematic course of instruction by an appropriate Federal law enforcement agency.' The memo interprets this to preclude CIA in‑house training for Access Control Officers (ACOs) and to mandate external training at agencies such as the FBI or the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Accredited Course of Training'
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'accredited course of training' is defined in the draft OMB cover letter as 'A systematic course of instruction by an appropriate Federal law enforcement agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition functions as an eligibility/authorization standard for granting arrest or firearms authority. The memorandum highlights that this definition would likely exclude agency‑conducted internal training programs unless they are conducted by or accredited through an 'appropriate Federal law enforcement agency.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to Carry a Firearm
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 4(a) ('Authority to Carry a Firearm') appears to require that officers who carry firearms 'must complete an accredited course of training in the carrying and use of firearms.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo reads this to imply firearms training must be taught by an appropriate Federal law enforcement agency. It notes that historically CIA firearms training has been provided by CIA instructors (accredited by the U.S. Secret Service) and that the OMB guideline could call that practice into question, creating significant logistical burdens if all training must be performed externally or in cooperation with other federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Protective Responsibility under 40 U.S.C. 318
rubrics_metrics.description: CIA signed a Memorandum of Agreement with GSA delegating protective responsibility for the CIA compound under 40 U.S.C. 318.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Security believes this delegation is authorized under the statute and that CIA may accept such a delegation 'without further Congressional legislation.' This functions as a legal standard supporting CIA's authority to assume protective responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation Requirements for New Civilian Guard Force (Access Control Officers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft guidelines affect the appropriate legal responsibility to implement the Agency's new civilian guard force (tentatively termed 'Access Control Officers' (ACOs)), including law enforcement training accreditation and firearms training authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implications include potential need to send ACOs to external accredited training, coordination with federal training providers, and significant resource/logistical impacts (e.g., numbers of personnel and geographic dispersion). The memo recommends obtaining an expeditious legal opinion and routing inquiries to the Policy and Plans Group to address these implementation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Rely on 'Appropriate Federal Law Enforcement Agency' for Accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple subsections of the draft OMB guidance hinge on courses being delivered or accredited by an 'appropriate Federal law enforcement agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion serves as an explicit limitation on what training counts as accredited; the memo treats it as an exclusionary standard (anti-pattern) for internal agency accreditation unless external accreditation/acceptance exists. Examples cited include FBI, FLETC, or accreditation via U.S. Secret Service training of instructors.
